explanation: Strongest on the class-name part of a constructor definition that repeats the class name (e.g. 'public Generic[[Repository]](', 'Vertice3f::Vertice3[[f]](') in Java/C#/C++. It also fires moderately to fairly strongly on assorted prose and math tokens (the space after 'Solve' in math problems, ' did', ' in', ' p' in statistics) with no shared theme.

Peaks on ' tilt' in Earth's-tilt/seasons text, and fires moderately on periodic/time things (2π, 'periodic', seconds in timestamps, time zones like EDT/AM). It also fires weakly to moderately on number slots after '=' or before a quantity in math and units text. Mostly a diffuse mixture.

Fires on the second subword token of foreign or rare proper nouns, especially ones starting with 'K'/'Kok'/'Hok'/'Sok' (Hokkaido, Kokkadave, Sokol, Kankakee, Hockenheim). It also fires on French ' plus', German ' aber', Czech diacritics, and some code tokens (Format, '[0'). A mixed set built around non-English name fragments.

Fires on a wide range of tokens: math/code operators (\frac '{', '%' modulo, ' by' in 'divided by'), version and path digits ('64', 'jdk-13.0.1'), '.twitter' in pic.twitter.com, and many ordinary prose words. No single theme can be seen.

Fires on word-initial 'D'-type fragments, mainly the abbreviation 'DM' (diabetes mellitus, DMH, DMRC) and the 'des/dif/dec(ou)/dé' prefixes in Romance-language and English words (desmanche, difundir, decoupled). Weaker on 'dp', 'DR', 'dys', 'diabetes'. The token itself matters, with little dependence on context.

Fires strongly on a very heterogeneous set of tokens: the space before the page number in 'Page: 1' court-document headers, tech-prose words (Step, extconf, Values, minified), and ordinary prose nouns and prepositions. No shared feature is apparent.

Fires on tokens in formal or legal register: lawyer listings like 'on the brief', 'pro se', 'trial', license boilerplate ('hope that', 'name of'), and math prompts ('factors of', 'common factor of'). It also fires on assorted technical words. Loosely about formal or boilerplate text, but scattered.

Fires on tokens inside boilerplate or header-like text: long whitespace runs in court captions, license headers ('either', 'or more', 'Zend Framework'), and Chinese characters in technical docs. It also fires on scattered prose tokens (commas, 'x' in dimensions, numbers). A mixture.

Fires on a mixture of tokens: the 'CIR/CU' fragments of 'CIRCUIT' in court headers, 'out of' (line/ordinary), whitespace or quotes in code alignment, the ';' after property declarations, and prepositions like 'by'/'para' after a verb. No coherent single theme.

Fires on a quantifier/determiner-like token in Vietnamese ('mọi', 'cả') and Chinese ('的情况下'). It also fires on digits in factor lists or numbers, code identifiers, and English words like 'my', 'you', 'THIS'. Mixed, with a weak lean toward 'all/most' quantifier contexts in non-English text.

Fires most consistently on ' to' in the Apache license phrase 'agreed to in writing' and on other license-header tokens ('license', '(the', 'SPDX...:', '@path'). Secondary firing on code identifiers (extends Component, newSprite.ID, _middleName) and some prose ('after adjustment for age').

Fires on 'duct' in 'reductase'/'reductant'/'reduction', and on second pieces of proper nouns or software names (Diffie, MS Word, Access, KGB, gnuplot, NHK). It also fires on the opening quote of an import path in JS ('from "axios"'). A mixture.

Fires on a middle subword piece of a multi-token word ('dig[[ress]]', 'art[[ikk]]elen', 'P[[unt]]ers', 'stop[[page]]', 'CERT[[IFY]]', 'app[[elle]]e', 'miss[[pell]]ings'), regardless of topic or language. A few whole-word hits (' article', 'Entry', ' point') are weaker exceptions.

Fires on the keyword that opens a nested or new code block: 'SELECT' right after '(' in SQL subqueries, and 'namespace', 'class', 'type', 'def', 'template', 'function' at the start of a declaration, especially inside another scope. It is weaker on '(function' callbacks and on 'the following' in license text.
